title: Units needed to graduate with a bachelor's degree (120)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Units needed to graduate with a bachelor's degree (120) (undergraduate students)

A bachelor's degree (B.A., B.S., or B.Mus.) requires a minimum of 120 semester units.
Bulletin text: "An undergraduate student who has completed all of the requirements for graduation and has a total of 120 semester units is eligible to graduate with a baccalaureate degree."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Units to Graduate

title: Residence units required at SF State (30)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Residence units required at SF State (30) (undergraduate students)

At least 30 units must be earned in residence at SF State, including 24 upper-division units and 12 units in the major.
Bulletin text: "Residence Requirement: 30 units minimum at SF State, including 24 units upper-division, and 12 units in the major (lower- or upper-division)."
Source: Degree Requirements > Unit Requirements

title: Upper-division GE units required in residence (9)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Upper-division GE units required in residence (9) (undergraduate students)

Nine of the 30 residence units must be earned in upper-division General Education.
Bulletin text: "Nine of these residence units must be earned in the Upper Division portion of the General Education program."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Residence Units Requirement

title: Upper-division units required for a bachelor's degree (30)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Upper-division units required for a bachelor's degree (30) (undergraduate students)

At least 30 upper-division units (courses numbered 300-699) are required for the bachelor's degree.
Bulletin text: "For the award of the baccalaureate degree, all students are required to complete a minimum of 30 upper-division units (courses numbered 300-699 at SF State)."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Upper-Division Units Requirement

title: Maximum community college transfer units (70)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum community college transfer units (70) (undergraduate students)

At most 70 semester units of community college work count toward the degree.
Bulletin text: "The University accepts a maximum of 70 semester units for work completed at a community college."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Credit for Community College Work

title: Maximum extension and correspondence units (24)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum extension and correspondence units (24) (undergraduate students)

At most 24 semester units of extension and correspondence credit count toward the degree.
Bulletin text: "The University accepts a maximum of 24 semester units of extension credit and correspondence courses towards award of a baccalaureate degree."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Credit for Extension and Correspondence Work

title: Maximum units by exam or evaluation (30)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units by exam or evaluation (30) (undergraduate students)

At most 30 units by examination or evaluation count toward the degree.
Bulletin text: "Maximum Units by Examination or Evaluation: 30 units."
Source: Degree Requirements > Unit Requirements > Maximum Unit Restrictions

title: Maximum CR/NC (pass/fail) units toward a bachelor's degree (24)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum CR/NC (pass/fail) units toward a bachelor's degree (24) (undergraduate students)

No more than 24 SF State units applied to the bachelor's degree may be graded CR (Credit). Major courses offered only as CR/NC don't count toward the 24.
Bulletin text: "Maximum Units CR/NC: No more than 24 units earned at SF State and applied toward the undergraduate degree may be taken for a grade of CR. Major courses only offered as CR/NC are not included in the 24 unit maximum."
Source: Degree Requirements > Unit Requirements > Maximum Unit Restrictions

title: Maximum 685 'Projects in Teaching' units (4)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum 685 'Projects in Teaching' units (4) (undergraduate students)

At most 4 units of courses numbered 685 titled 'Projects in Teaching...' apply to the bachelor's degree.
Bulletin text: "Maximum Units for Courses Numbered "685" and Titled "Projects in Teaching . . ." That may be Applied to the Baccalaureate Degree: 4 units."
Source: Degree Requirements > Unit Requirements > Maximum Unit Restrictions

title: Minimum GPA to graduate (2.0)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum GPA to graduate (2.0) (undergraduate students)

Graduation requires a 2.0 GPA or better in combined cumulative, SF State, and major coursework.
Bulletin text: "To be eligible for graduation, students must achieve a combined cumulative, SF State, and major GPA of 2.0 or better."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Minimum Grade-Point Average

title: General Education units required (43)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: General Education units required (43) (undergraduate students)

General Education requires at least 43 units.
Bulletin text: "General Education Requirements - 43 units minimum"
Source: Degree Requirements > Graduation Requirement in Writing Proficiency > General Education Requirements – 43 units minimum

title: Upper-division GE requirement (9 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Upper-division GE requirement (9 units) (undergraduate students)

Upper-division GE requires at least 9 units: one 3-unit course each in 2UD or 5UD (science/quantitative reasoning), 3UD (arts/humanities), and 4UD (social/behavioral sciences).
Bulletin text: "Upper-Division General Education - 9 Units Minimum"
Source: Upper-Division General Education > Upper-Division General Education — 9 Units Minimum > General Requirements

title: Prerequisites for upper-division GE courses
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Prerequisites for upper-division GE courses (undergraduate students)

Upper-division GE courses require 1A, 1B, 1C and Area 2 first; they're recommended after 60 units.
Bulletin text: "Minimally, all of these courses have a prerequisite of English Composition (1A), Critical Thinking (1B), Oral Communication (1C), and Mathematical Concepts and Quantitative Reasoning (2)."
Source: Upper-Division General Education > Upper-Division General Education — 9 Units Minimum > General Requirements

title: GE Area 1 English Communication requirement and minimum grade
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE Area 1 English Communication requirement and minimum grade (undergraduate students)

GE Area 1 (English Communication): at least 9 units, 3 each in 1A English Composition, 1B Critical Thinking, 1C Oral Communication. Every Area 1 course needs CR or C- or better.
Bulletin text: "Requirements: Students must complete a minimum of nine units in Area 1, including a minimum of three units in each of the following three areas: English Composition, Critical Thinking, and Oral Communication."
Source: Lower-Division General Education > Area 1: English Communication — 9 units

title: GE Area 3 Arts and Humanities requirement
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE Area 3 Arts and Humanities requirement (undergraduate students)

GE Area 3 (Arts and Humanities): at least 6 units, 3 in Arts (3A) and 3 in Humanities (3B).
Bulletin text: "Requirements: Students must complete a minimum of 6 units in Area 3 including three units in Arts (3a) and three units in Humanities (3B)."
Source: Lower-Division General Education > Area 3: Arts and Humanities — 6 units

title: GE Area 5 Physical and Biological Sciences requirement
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE Area 5 Physical and Biological Sciences requirement (undergraduate students)

GE Area 5 (Physical and Biological Sciences): at least 7 units, including 3 in physical science and 3 in biological science (plus a 1-unit lab, 5C).
Bulletin text: "Requirements: All students must complete a minimum of 7 units in Area 5, including a minimum of three units in each of the following two areas: Physical Science and Biological Science."
Source: Lower-Division General Education > Area 5: Physical and Biological Sciences — 7 units

title: GE requirements by area (units per area)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE requirements by area (units per area) (undergraduate students)

GE requirement table: 1A 3, 1B 3, 1C 3, 2 3, 3A 3, 3B 3, 4 6, 5A 3, 5B 3, 5C 1, 6 (Ethnic Studies, LD or UD) 3, 2UD/5UD 3, 3UD 3, 4UD 3. Area 4 also covers U.S. History (USH).
Bulletin text: "Students will fulfill USH through their Area 4 courses | | | |"
Source: Undergraduate Education > Introduction to General Education > General Education Requirements for all Baccalaureate Degrees

title: Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR, GW courses)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR, GW courses) (undergraduate students)

Every bachelor's program requires a Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) course, marked 'GW' after the number, passed with C- or better.
Bulletin text: "These courses are identified with a GW after the course number and must be completed with a grade of C- or better to meet the requirement."
Source: Degree Requirements > Graduation Requirement in Writing Proficiency

title: SF State Studies requirement (AERM, ESCA, GP, SJ)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: SF State Studies requirement (AERM, ESCA, GP, SJ) (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates must take courses covering all four SF State Studies areas: AERM, ESCA, GP and SJ. Courses may come from GE, major, minor or electives. Students with a verified AA-T/AS-T in a similar major are exempt.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students must complete courses that cover the four areas of SF State Studies: American Ethnic and Racial Minorities (AERM), Environmental Sustainability and Climate Action (ESCA), Global Perspectives (GP), and Social Justice (SJ)."
Source: Degree Requirements > Graduation Requirement in Writing Proficiency > SF State Studies Requirements

title: American Institutions requirement (U.S. History and Government)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: American Institutions requirement (U.S. History and Government) (undergraduate students)

American Institutions has two parts: U.S. History (USH) and U.S. and California Government (USG/CSLG).
Bulletin text: "The American Institutions requirement consists of two categories:"
Source: Degree Requirements > Graduation Requirement in Writing Proficiency > American Institutions Requirement

title: Complementary Studies requirement for B.A. degrees (12 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Complementary Studies requirement for B.A. degrees (12 units) (undergraduate students)

B.A. students may need at least 12 units of Complementary Studies outside the major's primary prefix.
Bulletin text: "Bachelor of Arts students may be required to complete at least 12 units of Complementary Studies outside of the primary prefix for the major."
Source: Complementary Studies > Complementary Studies: Bachelor of Arts Degrees (12 units)

title: Who is exempt from Complementary Studies
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Who is exempt from Complementary Studies (undergraduate students)

Complementary Studies is automatically met by completing two majors or a major plus a minor, and isn't required for B.Mus. or B.S. degrees.
Bulletin text: "Students who complete two majors or a major and a minor automatically complete the Complementary Studies requirement."
Source: Complementary Studies > Complementary Studies: Bachelor of Arts Degrees (12 units)

title: Deadline to declare a major (70 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Deadline to declare a major (70 units) (undergraduate students)

Students who enter as freshmen must declare a major by the time they complete 70 units.
Bulletin text: "Students who enter SF State as freshmen must declare a major by the time they complete 70 units."
Source: Major >

title: Minimum GPA in the major (2.0)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum GPA in the major (2.0) (undergraduate students)

The major requires a minimum 2.0 GPA; some majors set higher grade minimums.
Bulletin text: "Grade Point Average Students must have a minimum 2.0 grade point average (GPA) in their major."
Source: Major >

title: Can a GE course also count for my major
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Can a GE course also count for my major (undergraduate students)

Any number of GE courses may also count toward the major, but their units count once toward the 120.
Bulletin text: "Duplicate Use of Credit Between the Major and GE If applicable, an unlimited number of courses used to meet General Education requirements may be used to fulfill major requirements."
Source: Major >

title: Which requirements apply after changing majors
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Which requirements apply after changing majors (undergraduate students)

When you declare or change a major after admission, you follow the major requirements in effect at the time of the declaration/change.
Bulletin text: "Change of Major Students who change their major after being admitted or who declare a major after being admitted with an undeclared major must fulfill the major requirements in effect at the time they declare or change their major."
Source: Major >

title: Minor requirements: minimum units, residence, GPA
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minor requirements: minimum units, residence, GPA (undergraduate students)

A minor requires at least 12 units; at least half must be taken at SF State and at least 6 units must be upper-division; 2.0 GPA in the minor; no major and minor in the same discipline.
Bulletin text: "Minimum Units A minor must include a minimum of 12 units."
Source: Minor >

title: Minor units that must be taken at SF State
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minor units that must be taken at SF State (undergraduate students)

At least half the minor's units must be taken at SF State and at least 6 must be upper-division.
Bulletin text: "Upper-Division/Residence Units At least half of the units making up the minor must be taken at SF State, and at least 6 units must be upper-division."
Source: Minor >

title: Time limit for undergraduate degree courses (seven-year rule)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Time limit for undergraduate degree courses (seven-year rule) (undergraduate students)

No general time limit for undergraduate units, but departments may require retaking major/minor/certificate courses taken more than 7 years before graduation.
Bulletin text: "However, if any course required for the major, minor, or certificate was taken more than seven years prior to graduation, then departments and programs may require students to retake that course or demonstrate currency in that subject."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Time Limit to Complete Requirements for Undergraduate Degree

title: Class level by units: freshman, sophomore, junior, senior
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Class level by units: freshman, sophomore, junior, senior (undergraduate students)

Class level by earned units: Freshman 0-29, Sophomore 30-59, Junior 60-89, Senior 90+.
Bulletin text: "The class level of students is determined according to units completed (earned units) as follows:"
Source: Policies and Procedures > Class Level of Students

title: Average full-time undergraduate course load (15 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Average full-time undergraduate course load (15 units) (undergraduate students)

15 units is an average full-time undergraduate semester load.
Bulletin text: "units are considered an average semester course load for full-time undergraduate students."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Normal course load per semester (undergraduate and graduate)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Normal course load per semester (undergraduate and graduate) (all students)

Normal load: undergraduates 12-15 units per fall/spring semester (8 in summer); graduates 9-12 (7 in summer). Expect two hours of preparation for every hour of class.
Bulletin text: "During spring and fall, the normal academic load for undergraduates is 12 to 15 units per semester and 8 units in the summer. For graduates, the normal load during spring and fall is from 9 to 12 units per semester and 7 units during the summer."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Academic Load

title: Maximum units per semester for undergraduates (19)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units per semester for undergraduates (19) (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates can register for at most 19 units in a fall or spring semester (up to 8 of them wait-listed). Going above this cap needs the Exceed Maximum Units Petition.
Bulletin text: "During priority registration, students may register for a maximum of 19 units of enrolled, including 8 units of wait-listed courses."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Maximum units per semester at registration for graduate students (16)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units per semester at registration for graduate students (16) (graduate students)

Graduate students can register for at most 16 units, including up to 9 wait-listed units.
Bulletin text: "Graduate students may register for a maximum of 16 units of enrolled, including 9 units of wait-listed courses."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Maximum units per semester on academic notice/probation (13)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units per semester on academic notice/probation (13) (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates on academic notice may enroll in at most 13 units per semester while their GPA is below 2.0. An advisor can approve an exception by petition.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students on academic notice may enroll in a maximum of 13 units (this does not go into effect until a student’s second semester on academic notice)."
Conflicting bulletin text (Academic Standards): "Undergraduate students who are on academic notice can enroll in a maximum of 13 units per semester while their GPA is below 2.0 (Academic Senate Policy S23-275)." — The Academic Standards page applies the cap while the GPA is below 2.0 and doesn't mention the second-semester start.
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Maximum summer session units for undergraduates
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum summer session units for undergraduates (undergraduate students)

Summer maximums (undergraduate): 7 units in a 5-week session, 9 in an 8-week, 12 in a 10-week, 14 across all summer sessions combined (including 8 wait-listed).
Bulletin text: "During the summer semester, undergraduate students may enroll in a maximum of 7 units in a five-week summer session, 9 units in an eight-week session, 12 units in a ten-week summer session, and a maximum of 14 units in any combination of summer semester sessions, including 8 units of wait-listed courses."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: How to take more than the maximum units (Exceed Maximum Units Petition)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: How to take more than the maximum units (Exceed Maximum Units Petition) (undergraduate students)

To exceed the maximum, undergraduates need a cumulative SF State GPA of 3.0+ and an approved Exceed Maximum Units Petition (major advisor, department chair, college dean).
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students who want to enroll in more than the maximum units listed above must have a cumulative SF State grade point average of 3.0 or better and secure approval via the Exceed Maximum Units Petition."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Taking 25 or more units in a semester
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Taking 25 or more units in a semester (undergraduate students)

Enrolling in 25 or more units in one semester requires approval from the advisor, college dean, and Dean of Undergraduate Education and Academic Planning.
Bulletin text: "Students who wish to enroll in 25 or more units in one semester must receive the approval of their advisor, their college dean, and the Dean of Undergraduate Education and Academic Planning using the Exceed Maximum Units Petition."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Maximum Units in One Semester

title: Minimum units per semester for international (F-1) students
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum units per semester for international (F-1) students (all students)

International (F-1) students must carry at least 12 units (undergraduate) or 8 units (graduate) each fall and spring.
Bulletin text: "For international students in F1 visa status, immigration regulations require a minimum academic load of 12 units for undergraduates and 8 units for graduates for spring and fall semesters."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Academic Load

title: Full-time, three-quarter and half-time units (enrollment verification)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Full-time, three-quarter and half-time units (enrollment verification) (all students)

Enrollment status (used for enrollment verification, including financial aid): undergraduates are full time at 12-19 units, three-quarter time at 9-11, half time at 6-8, less than half time at 1-5. Graduate students are full time at 12 units, or 8 units if all are 300-level or above.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduates | Full Time | 12–19 units |"
Source: Policies and Procedures > Enrollment Verification

title: Full-time, three-quarter and half-time units for the Pell Grant
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Full-time, three-quarter and half-time units for the Pell Grant (undergraduate students)

For the Pell Grant: full-time = 12 units, three-quarter time = 9-11, half-time = 6-8 (award prorated). Other aid programs set their own unit rules.
Bulletin text: "Enrollment requirement: full time = 12 units; three-quarter time = 9-11 units; half-time = 6-8 units."
Source: Student Financial Aid > Program Highlights

title: Full-time units for graduate students
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Full-time units for graduate students (graduate students)

Graduate full-time in fall/spring: 6.1+ units for fee purposes, 8+ for financial aid and international students; typical load 9-12.
Bulletin text: "For those receiving financial aid, 8 units and above"
Source: Graduate Student Registration > Full-Time Unit Load for Graduate Students > Fall and Spring Semesters

title: Maximum units per semester for graduate students (16, petition above)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units per semester for graduate students (16, petition above) (graduate students)

Graduate maximum with advisor permission is 16 units; more than 16 needs GPA 3.25+ and a petition. In general a post-baccalaureate student can't exceed 18 units, except in cohorted professional programs.
Bulletin text: "The maximum unit load with the permission of the designated faculty advisor is 16 units."
Source: Graduate Student Registration > Full-Time Unit Load for Graduate Students > Fall and Spring Semesters

title: Maximum summer units for graduate students
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum summer units for graduate students (graduate students)

Graduate summer maximums: 6 units in a 5-week session, 9 in an 8- or 10-week session, 11 across all summer sessions.
Bulletin text: "Graduate students may enroll in a maximum of 6 units in a five-week summer session, 9 units in the eight or ten-week summer session, and 11 units in any combination of summer sessions (R1, R2, R3, and R4)."
Source: Graduate Student Registration > Full-Time Unit Load for Graduate Students > Summer Semester

title: Full-time units for VA education benefits
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Full-time units for VA education benefits (all students)

For VA benefits, undergraduates must complete 12+ units and graduates 8+ upper-division/graduate units (9+ if any lower-division) per term for maximum benefits.
Bulletin text: "For certification under the Veterans Readjustment Benefits Act of 1966 (Public Law 89–358), undergraduates must register for and complete 12 or more semester units of credit to receive maximum benefits."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Enrollment Verification > Winter Semester – Veterans Academic Load > Veterans and Dependents of Veterans

title: Deadline to add a class (first three weeks, permission number)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Deadline to add a class (first three weeks, permission number) (all students)

Courses can be added with an instructor-issued permission number during the first three weeks of the semester.
Bulletin text: "If the student has paid sufficient fees and has instructor approval, they may add courses via the SF State Gateway at gateway.sfsu.edu with instructor assigned permission numbers during the first three weeks of the semester."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Registration for Classes > Adding Courses after Instruction Begins

title: Deadline to drop a class without a W (first three weeks)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Deadline to drop a class without a W (first three weeks) (all students)

During the first three weeks, courses can be dropped without restriction or penalty; drops don't appear on the transcript or count toward the withdrawal limit.
Bulletin text: "During the first three weeks of instruction, students are permitted to drop classes without restriction or academic penalty."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Registration for Classes > Dropping Courses after Instruction Begins

title: Withdrawing from a class in weeks 4-12 (W grade)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Withdrawing from a class in weeks 4-12 (W grade) (all students)

Weeks 4-12: withdrawal requires serious and compelling reasons plus instructor and department chair approval; results in a W (not in GPA).
Bulletin text: "During the fourth through the twelfth week of instruction, students may request to withdraw from courses for serious and compelling reasons, as specified by the student."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Withdrawing from a Course or Courses

title: Withdrawing from a class after week 12 (serious circumstances only)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Withdrawing from a class after week 12 (serious circumstances only) (all students)

Week 13 to end of instruction: withdrawal only for circumstances clearly beyond the student's control (e.g., accident, serious illness) when an Incomplete isn't practicable, with documentation and instructor, chair and dean approval. These late withdrawals don't count toward the 18-unit limit.
Bulletin text: "From the thirteenth week through the last week of instruction, students may only request to withdraw in cases, such as an accident or serious illness, where the cause of withdrawal is due to circumstances clearly beyond the student's control and the assignment of an Incomplete is not practicable."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Withdrawing from a Course or Courses

title: Withdrawal limit: 18 units over your SF State career
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Withdrawal limit: 18 units over your SF State career (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates may withdraw from at most 18 units over their entire SF State career. Withdrawing from a whole semester, CPaGE classes, and late withdrawals approved for circumstances beyond the student's control don't count.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduates may withdraw from a maximum of 18 units throughout their entire SF State undergraduate career (see Grading Policy)."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Withdrawing from a Course or Courses

title: Last day to request a withdrawal
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Last day to request a withdrawal (all students)

All withdrawal requests must be submitted by the last day of instruction.
Bulletin text: "Academic Policy requires that all requests to withdraw from a course must be submitted no later than the last day of instruction of that term."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Withdrawing from a Course or Courses > Appeals for Requests to Withdraw > Appeal of the Deadline to Submit a Request for Withdrawal (formerly known as retroactive withdrawal)

title: What doesn't count toward the 18-unit withdrawal limit
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: What doesn't count toward the 18-unit withdrawal limit (undergraduate students)

Total-semester withdrawals and classes taken through CPaGE don't count toward the 18-unit withdrawal limit.
Bulletin text: "This does not include total semester withdrawals of all courses or classes taken in CPaGE (College of Professional and Global Education)."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > IV. Additional guidance and details on the use of specialized grading symbols: I, RP, WU, and WM > D. Use of WM Grade

title: When you must apply for readmission after not enrolling
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: When you must apply for readmission after not enrolling (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates who are away too long must apply for readmission. The bulletin is inconsistent: the policies page says three consecutive semesters (excluding summer); the readmission page says two. Plan on two to be safe and confirm with the Registrar.
Bulletin text: "Students who do not enroll for three consecutive semesters (excluding summer) must apply for readmission to the University."
Conflicting bulletin text (Readmission & Special Sessions): "Former students of the University must apply for readmission if they have been absent for two consecutive semesters (excluding winter and summer sessions)." — The readmission page says two consecutive semesters.
Source: Policies and Procedures > Withdrawal Policy > Cancellation of Registration and Withdrawals

title: Readmission for graduate students after time away
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Readmission for graduate students after time away (graduate students)

Graduate students who leave for two or more consecutive semesters (not counting summer), or attend another college meanwhile, must reapply through Cal State Apply and to their program.
Bulletin text: "Students who leave the University for two or more consecutive semesters (not including summer session), or who have attended another college or university during their absence, must reapply for admission to the University through CAL STATE APPLY, pay the application fee, submit any new transcripts other than the SF State transcripts, and reapply to the program in which they were enrolled."
Source: Graduate Student Registration > Continuous Enrollment Requirements > Prior to Enrolling in the Culminating Experience

title: Auditing a class
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Auditing a class (all students)

Auditors pay the same fees; switching audit to credit must happen by the add deadline; credit to audit isn't allowed after week 2 per the policies page (the grading page's AU definition says week 3).
Bulletin text: "A student who is enrolled for credit may not change to audit after the second week of instruction."
Conflicting bulletin text (Grading Information and Systems): "W: (Withdrawal) Indicates that the student was permitted to withdraw from the course after the third week of instruction with the approval of the instructor and appropriate campus officials." — The AU grade definition on the grading page says the third week.
Source: Policies and Procedures > Auditing Courses

title: Leave of absence (Planned Educational Leave)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Leave of absence (Planned Educational Leave) (all students)

Continuing students can be absent up to two consecutive fall/spring semesters and keep continuing status; longer absences need a Planned Educational Leave (up to two academic years), which must be for something relevant to the program. For undergraduates, health, financial and personal reasons aren't accepted; the graduate rules differ (see the graduate policies page).
Bulletin text: "Continuing students can be absent up to two consecutive fall or spring semesters during a specific academic year and maintain their eligibility."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Planned Educational Leave of Absence

title: Reasons not accepted for an undergraduate leave of absence
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Reasons not accepted for an undergraduate leave of absence (undergraduate students)

A Planned Educational Leave isn't granted for health, financial, or other personal reasons, or to attend another school; those students reapply for admission instead.
Bulletin text: "Requests for health, financial, or other personal reasons, or matriculation at another institution are not recognized for the purpose of granting a leave of absence."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Planned Educational Leave of Absence

title: Grade points per letter grade (GPA scale)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Grade points per letter grade (GPA scale) (all students)

Grade points per unit: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, B- 2.7, C+ 2.3, C 2.0, C- 1.7, D+ 1.3, D 1.0, D- 0.7, F 0, IC 0, WU 0. W, I, AU, RP, RD, CR, NC carry no grade points. There is no A+.
Bulletin text: "No other grading symbol, including W, I, AU, RP, RD, CR, and NC, carries grade point credit."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > VI. Grade Points

title: How GPA is calculated
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: How GPA is calculated (all students)

GPA = total grade points / total units attempted in A-F graded courses (adjusted by the course repeat policy).
Bulletin text: "Grade point averages are determined by dividing the total number of grade points earned by the total number of units attempted in courses in which A–F grades are assigned."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > V. Grade Point Average

title: What a CR (credit) grade means
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: What a CR (credit) grade means (all students)

CR means A through C- work in an undergraduate course, or A through B- in a graduate course.
Bulletin text: "CR: (Credit) Performance of the student in an undergraduate-level course has been equivalent to grades A through C-; performance of the student in a graduate level course has been equivalent to grades A through B-."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > II. Grading Symbol Definitions

title: Deadline to switch to CR/NC (pass/fail) grading
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Deadline to switch to CR/NC (pass/fail) grading (all students)

The deadline to change grading option (e.g., to CR/NC) is one week before the last day of instruction.
Bulletin text: "Students must elect to change their grading option by the Grading Option deadline each semester, which is one week before the last day of instruction."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > III. Grading Systems

title: CR/NC limit for master's degrees (30% of ATC units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: CR/NC limit for master's degrees (30% of ATC units) (graduate students)

For a master's degree, at most 30% of Advancement to Candidacy units may be CR.
Bulletin text: "For students working toward a master's degree, no more than 30% of the units used on the Advancement to Candidacy, including transfer work, may be taken for CR grades."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > III. Grading Systems

title: Incomplete (I) grade rules and deadline
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Incomplete (I) grade rules and deadline (all students)

An Incomplete (I) requires passing work and normally 75%+ of coursework done. It must be made up within one calendar year, or it becomes IC, which counts as F.
Bulletin text: "An incomplete must normally be made up within one calendar year immediately following the end of the term during which it was assigned, however upon consultation with the student, the course instructor does have the discretion to shorten this period of time to less than one calendar year."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > IV. Additional guidance and details on the use of specialized grading symbols: I, RP, WU, and WM > A. Use of Incomplete Authorized (I) Grade

title: What a WU (unauthorized withdrawal) grade means
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: What a WU (unauthorized withdrawal) grade means (all students)

WU (unauthorized withdrawal) counts as a failing grade in the GPA.
Bulletin text: "The WU symbol shall be identified as a failing grade in the transcript legend, and shall be counted as units attempted but not passed in computing the grade point average."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > IV. Additional guidance and details on the use of specialized grading symbols: I, RP, WU, and WM > C. Use of Withdrawal Unauthorized (WU) Grade

title: How many times can I repeat a course
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: How many times can I repeat a course (undergraduate students)

Undergraduates can't repeat a course passed with C or better (or CR) unless it's repeatable for credit. A course with a grade below C (including W, WU, etc.) may be repeated only once more.
Bulletin text: "An undergraduate student who has received a grade in a course that is lower than C, including AU, IC, RD, RP, W, and WU, may repeat that course only once more."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Repeating Courses

title: Grade forgiveness when repeating a course (16 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Grade forgiveness when repeating a course (16 units) (undergraduate students)

Up to 16 units of SF State coursework can be repeated for grade forgiveness (the lower grade is excluded from the GPA). It doesn't apply to academic dishonesty.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students may repeat a maximum of 16 units of coursework taken at San Francisco State University for the purpose of excluding the original grade from grade point determination."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grade Forgiveness Policy > Summary of the Grade Forgiveness Policy

title: Maximum units of repeated courses (28)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum units of repeated courses (28) (undergraduate students)

After repeating 28 units of SF State coursework, undergraduates can't repeat more courses (except those repeatable for credit).
Bulletin text: "An undergraduate student cannot repeat any courses once they have repeated 28 units of SF State units unless the course is described in the Bulletin as repeatable for credit."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Repeating Courses

title: Can a course be repeated for more credit
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Can a course be repeated for more credit (all students)

Courses can't be repeated for additional credit unless the course description says so.
Bulletin text: "Unless otherwise stated in the course descriptions in the current SF State Bulletin, courses may not be repeated for additional units of credit."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Repeating Courses

title: Repeating a course as a graduate student
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Repeating a course as a graduate student (graduate students)

Graduate students can repeat a course graded below B- (or IC, W, WU) once, if the program permits. Both grades stay on the transcript and are averaged. (The general policies page says 'lower than B', so a B- is ambiguous.)
Bulletin text: "A graduate student who has received a grade of B– or better, or a grade of CR, may not repeat a course unless the course is described in the current SF State Bulletin as repeatable for credit."
Conflicting bulletin text (Policies and Procedures): "Graduate students who receive a grade lower than B, including AU, IC, RD, RP, W, and WU, may repeat that course only once more." — The policies page sets the repeat threshold at lower than B.
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > Academic Standards > Repeat of Courses as a Graduate Student

title: Good academic standing (GPA 2.0)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Good academic standing (GPA 2.0) (undergraduate students)

Good academic standing means a 2.0 GPA or better.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students with a 2.0-grade point average (GPA) or better are said to be in good academic standing."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Good Standing

title: Academic notice (probation) for GPA below 2.0
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Academic notice (probation) for GPA below 2.0 (undergraduate students)

An SF State or combined cumulative GPA below 2.0 puts an undergraduate on academic notice; a second semester below 2.0 makes them subject to disqualification (mandatory advising, registration hold).
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students with an SF State and/or combined cumulative GPA of less than 2.0 are not in good academic standing and will be placed on academic notice (Academic Senate Policy S23-275)."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Academic Notice

title: Academic disqualification GPA thresholds by class level
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Academic disqualification GPA thresholds by class level (undergraduate students)

Only students already on academic notice or subject to disqualification can be disqualified. It happens before the next fall/spring term when the term GPA is below 2.0 AND the SF State or combined cumulative GPA is below the class-level floor: 1.50 freshman (<30 units), 1.70 sophomore (30-59), 1.85 junior (60-89), 1.95 senior (90+). Freshmen get an extra (third) semester first. A term GPA of 2.0+ prevents disqualification.
Bulletin text: "Undergraduate students on academic notice or subject to disqualification are academically disqualified before the start of the subsequent fall or spring semester if their term GPA is less than a 2.0 and their SF State and/or combined cumulative GPA fall below the thresholds listed below:"
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Subject to Disqualification and Academic Disqualification

title: Returning after academic disqualification
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Returning after academic disqualification (undergraduate students)

Disqualified students must raise SF State and combined GPAs to 2.0 (SF State GPA via Open University). Within one year they can ask the Registrar for reinstatement; after more than two semesters they must apply for admission again.
Bulletin text: "Students who have been academically disqualified from SF State must raise their SF State and combined cumulative GPAs to a 2.0 or better to be reinstated or readmitted to SF State."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Readmission of Disqualified Students

title: Dean's List requirements (GPA 3.25, 12 units)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Dean's List requirements (GPA 3.25, 12 units) (undergraduate students)

Dean's List: 12+ A-F graded units completed in the semester with a semester GPA of 3.25 or better.
Bulletin text: "The student attained a GPA of 3.25 or better for the semester."
Source: Scholastic Distinction > Semester Dean’s List

title: Graduation honors GPA: cum laude, magna cum laude, summa cum laude
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Graduation honors GPA: cum laude, magna cum laude, summa cum laude (undergraduate students)

Graduation honors by cumulative GPA: cum laude 3.50-3.69, magna cum laude 3.70-3.84, summa cum laude 3.85+. GPA is not rounded.
Bulletin text: "A student whose GPA is 3.85 or greater shall graduate summa cum laude."
Source: Scholastic Distinction > Graduation with Honors

title: Minimum units for master's and doctoral degrees
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum units for master's and doctoral degrees (graduate students)

Minimum units: master's (M.A., M.S., M.P.H., M.M.) 30; M.F.A. 60; doctorates (Ed.D., D.P.T.) 60.
Bulletin text: "Master’s degrees (M.A., M.S., M.P.H., M.M.): 30 units"
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > Graduate Program Requirements > Graduate Program Unit Requirements

title: Minimum GPA for graduate students and ATC course grades
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum GPA for graduate students and ATC course grades (graduate students)

Graduate students need a 3.0 GPA in all post-baccalaureate SF State work and on the Advancement to Candidacy (ATC); non-supervisory ATC courses need B- or better. (Another section lists A through C and CR as acceptable on the ATC; programs may require B or better.)
Bulletin text: "All non-supervisory courses listed on the ATC must have a grade of B- or higher."
Conflicting bulletin text (Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures): "Only the grades of A, A–, B+, B, B–, C+, C, and CR are acceptable in courses on the Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) form." — The Satisfactory Scholarship section lists C+ and C as acceptable on the ATC.
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > The Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) > Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) Requirements

title: Graduate academic probation (GPA below 3.0)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Graduate academic probation (GPA below 3.0) (graduate students)

Graduate students go on academic notice/probation if overall, SF State or semester GPA falls below 3.0.
Bulletin text: "Students will be placed on academic notice/probation if the overall, SF State, or semester GPA falls below 3.0 (B)."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > Graduate Student Academic Standing > Academic Notice/Probation

title: Time limit to finish a master's degree (seven years)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Time limit to finish a master's degree (seven years) (graduate students)

Master's and doctoral degrees must be completed within seven years; one extension of up to one year may be requested.
Bulletin text: "Title 5 of the California Code of Regulations requires that a master’s or doctoral degree shall be completed in no more than seven years."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > The Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) > Progress Toward Degree

title: Minimum progress for graduate students (6 units a year)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Minimum progress for graduate students (6 units a year) (graduate students)

Graduate students must complete at least 6 units each year (excluding summer).
Bulletin text: "Graduate students must make continuous satisfactory progress toward their degree by completing a minimum of 6 units each year, not including the summer session."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > The Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) > Progress Toward Degree

title: Residence units for a master's degree (21 of 30)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Residence units for a master's degree (21 of 30) (graduate students)

At least 21 of 30 master's units must be taken in residence (proportionally more for larger programs).
Bulletin text: "At least 21 of 30 units must be taken in residence on this campus or proportionally more for programs that exceed 30 units."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > The Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) > Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) Requirements

title: Transfer units allowed toward a master's degree (9)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Transfer units allowed toward a master's degree (9) (graduate students)

At most 9 semester units of transfer/CPaGE coursework may apply to a 30-unit graduate program (more for 45+ unit programs).
Bulletin text: "At the discretion of the department faculty, with support of the Dean of Graduate Studies, a maximum of 9 semester units, including any combination of transfer units or coursework through the College of Professional & Global Education, may be used to meet the requirements of a 30 unit program, or proportionally more for a program requiring 45 or more units."
Source: Graduate Application and Admissions Procedures > Transfer Credit from Other Institutions

title: Open University units allowed toward a master's degree (6)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Open University units allowed toward a master's degree (6) (graduate students)

At most 6 Open University units may apply to a 30-unit master's (no more than 12 for larger degrees).
Bulletin text: "Students may apply no more than 6 units taken through Open University enrollment toward a 30 unit master’s degree, or proportionally more for a higher unit degree (no more than 12 units), provided they are admitted to the program, and the units are accepted by the graduate coordinator of the degree program at the time of admission."
Source: Graduate Student Registration > College of Professional & Global Education > Open University

title: Using courses taken as an undergraduate toward a graduate degree
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Using courses taken as an undergraduate toward a graduate degree (graduate students)

Up to 9 upper-division or 12 graduate units (max 12 total) taken as an undergraduate can count toward a graduate program if not used for the bachelor's degree, and only units graded B or better.
Bulletin text: "Credit for Graduate Courses Completed as an Undergraduate: Up to 9 units of upper-division or up to 12 units of graduate work (not to exceed a total of 12 units) completed as an undergraduate may be counted toward a graduate program ONLY if the work was taken before the bachelor’s degree was earned and not counted toward the undergraduate degree."
Source: Graduate Application and Admissions Procedures > Credits Taken Prior to Admission to a Graduate Program at San Francisco State

title: SF State Scholars combined bachelor's and master's units (150)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: SF State Scholars combined bachelor's and master's units (150) (graduate students)

SF State Scholars (combined bachelor's + master's) requires at least 150 units total (120 + 30).
Bulletin text: "The minimum unit requirement to obtain both undergraduate and graduate degrees is 150 units (120 units and 30 units, respectively)."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > Graduate Program Requirements > Master’s Degree Requirements > San Francisco State Scholars Programs (FastTrack) > Award of San Francisco State Scholars Bachelor’s and Master’s Degrees:

title: GE Area 2 math/quantitative reasoning minimum grade
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE Area 2 math/quantitative reasoning minimum grade (undergraduate students)

GE Area 2 (quantitative reasoning) courses need CR or C- or better.
Bulletin text: "Area 2 courses must be completed with a grade of CR or C- or better to fulfill the General Education requirement."
Source: Lower-Division General Education > Area 2: Mathematical Concepts and Quantitative Reasoning (3 units required) [Formerly B4] > Summary of Quantitative Reasoning Requirements

title: GE Area 4 Social and Behavioral Sciences rules
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE Area 4 Social and Behavioral Sciences rules (undergraduate students)

The three Area 4 courses (two lower-division, one upper-division) must span at least two disciplines; first-time freshmen take one lower-division Area 4 course that meets U.S. History.
Bulletin text: "The three courses taken in Area 4 (one upper-division and two lower-division) must be in at least two different disciplines."
Source: Lower-Division General Education > Area 4: Social and Behavioral Sciences — 6 units [Formerly Area D]

title: Catalog rights: which bulletin's requirements apply to me
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Catalog rights: which bulletin's requirements apply to me (undergraduate students)

With continuous attendance, students may choose the graduation requirements in effect when they began study, when they entered SF State, or when they graduate.
Bulletin text: "A student, except a classified graduate student, who remains in continuous attendance in regular sessions and continuing in the same curriculum at any campus, in any of the California Community Colleges or in any combination of California Community Colleges and campuses of the California State University, may, for purposes of meeting graduation requirements, elect to meet the graduation requirements for San Francisco State University in effect (1) at the time they began their study, (2) at the time they entered the CSU campus from which they graduate, or (3) at the time they graduate from the CSU."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Observance of Bulletin Requirements

title: Continuous attendance definition for catalog rights
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Continuous attendance definition for catalog rights (undergraduate students)

Continuous attendance (for catalog rights) means attending at least one semester or two quarters each calendar year.
Bulletin text: "Continuous attendance for purposes of Bulletin requirements is defined as matriculated attendance in at least one semester or two quarters each calendar year."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Observance of Bulletin Requirements

title: Maximum total transfer units from all sources (90)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Maximum total transfer units from all sources (90) (undergraduate students)

No more than 90 semester units may be transferred in from all sources combined (because 30 units must be earned in residence).
Bulletin text: "Given the university's 30-semester (45-quarter) unit residency requirement, no more than a total of 90 semester (135 quarter) units may be transferred into the university from all sources."
Source: Transfer Students > Transfer Policies of California State University

title: Cal-GETC certification for transfer students
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Cal-GETC certification for transfer students (undergraduate students)

California Community Colleges can certify up to 34 semester units of Cal-GETC, which fulfills lower-division GE.
Bulletin text: "California Community Colleges can certify up to 34 semester (45 quarter) units of General Education Transfer Curriculum (Cal-GETC) for transfer students to fulfill lower-division general education requirements for any CSU prior to transfer."
Source: Transfer Students > Transfer Policies of California State University

title: Double major rules
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Double major rules (undergraduate students)

Students may complete two majors; courses that clearly overlap can count for both, but units count once toward 120. Apply for both in one degree application.
Bulletin text: "Duplicate Use of Credit Between Majors Students who complete two majors may count the same courses for both majors where there is a clearly stated overlap in the Bulletin requirements."
Source: Major >

title: Double major: one degree, one diploma, one fee
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Double major: one degree, one diploma, one fee (undergraduate students)

Double majors in the same degree type (e.g. two B.A. majors) get one degree and one diploma, with one $100 application fee.
Bulletin text: "Double majors leading to the same baccalaureate degree (B.A. or B.S.) do not constitute separate baccalaureate degrees, and only one degree and one diploma will be awarded."
Source: Graduation and Commencement > Graduation Information and Application Process for the Bachelor’s Degree > One Degree with Multiple Majors and/or Minors

title: Can courses count for both my major and minor
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Can courses count for both my major and minor (undergraduate students)

Courses may count toward both a major and a minor where the bulletin shows overlap (units count once). Minor and GE courses can overlap without limit.
Bulletin text: "Duplicate Use of Credit Between Major and Minor Courses may count for both a major and a minor where there is a clearly stated overlap in the Bulletin requirements."
Source: Minor >

title: Second bachelor's degree requirements
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Second bachelor's degree requirements (undergraduate students)

Students who already hold a bachelor's degree and are admitted for a second one only complete the new major's courses, not GE or other graduation requirements.
Bulletin text: "Students who have previously earned a baccalaureate or higher degree from an institutionally accredited college or university will not have to complete any GE or additional graduation requirements."
Source: Undergraduate Education > Second Baccalaureate Degree

title: Reapplying for graduation if you don't finish
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Reapplying for graduation if you don't finish (undergraduate students)

Students who don't finish in the term they applied for must reapply for graduation and pay the $100 fee again.
Bulletin text: "Students will need to reapply for graduation, pay the $100 application for graduation fee and demonstrate that all degree requirements have been met no later than the semester of actual completion of the outstanding requirement(s)."
Source: Graduation and Commencement > Commencement Ceremony and Graduation Approval > Graduation Ceremony

title: CR/NC limits in the major
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: CR/NC limits in the major (undergraduate students)

Departments may limit how many major courses can be taken CR/NC.
Bulletin text: "Departments may limit the number of courses in a major that can be graded CR/NC."
Source: Grading Information and Systems > Grading Information > III. Grading Systems

title: Taking a course a third time
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Taking a course a third time (all students)

Taking a course a third time or more requires the instructor's and department chair's consent (sometimes the dean or the Board of Appeals and Review too).
Bulletin text: "Exceptions to repeat a course for 3 or more times require the consent of the instructor and department chair in which the course is offered."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Repeating Courses

title: Academic renewal (removing old grades from GPA)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Academic renewal (removing old grades from GPA) (undergraduate students)

Academic renewal can disregard up to two semesters of old work if 5 years have passed and the student has since earned 15 units at 3.0, 30 at 2.5, or 45 at 2.0 in residence.
Bulletin text: "Five years have elapsed since the most recent work to be disregarded was completed, and"
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Academic Renewal

title: Administrative disqualification after three semesters on notice
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Administrative disqualification after three semesters on notice (undergraduate students)

Students on continuous academic notice or subject to disqualification for three semesters (not counting summer) may be administratively disqualified.
Bulletin text: "Students who have been on continuous academic notice and/or subject to disqualification for three continuous semesters may be administratively disqualified at the end of their third semester."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Administrative Academic Disqualification

title: Administrative academic notice for 15 units of No Credit
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Administrative academic notice for 15 units of No Credit (all students)

Repeated failure to progress, including 15 units of No Credit, can lead to administrative academic notice.
Bulletin text: "Repeated failure to progress toward the stated degree objective, or another program objective, including that resulting from assignment of 15 units of No Credit, when such failure appears to be due to circumstances within the control of the student."
Source: Academic Standards > Undergraduate Students > Administrative Academic Notice

title: AP U.S. History credit for American Institutions
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: AP U.S. History credit for American Institutions (undergraduate students)

An AP U.S. History score of 3+ satisfies the U.S. History requirement; no AP exam satisfies California state and local government.
Bulletin text: "A score of 3 or higher on the Advanced Placement examination in U.S. History will satisfy the U.S. History requirement."
Source: American Institutions > U.S. History > Advanced Placement (AP) Examinations

title: No duplicate credit for AP/IB/CLEP and coursework
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: No duplicate credit for AP/IB/CLEP and coursework (undergraduate students)

Exam credit (AP/IB/CLEP) isn't awarded twice for equivalent exams or coursework.
Bulletin text: "Students will not be awarded duplicate credit if they have previously completed or subsequently complete equivalent exams or college-level coursework."
Source: AP – IB – CLEP Examinations > Standardized External Examinations

title: Credit by examination (challenge a course)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Credit by examination (challenge a course) (undergraduate students)

Credit by examination is undergraduate-only, capped at 30 units (6 of which can count as residence), and requires enrollment in at least one other course.
Bulletin text: "Only undergraduate credit may be earned with a maximum limit of 30 units, 6 of which can be earned for residence credit."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Unit Requirements > Credit for Prior Experiential Learning

title: Taking classes at another school at the same time (unit load)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Taking classes at another school at the same time (unit load) (all students)

Units taken at all schools combined in a term can't exceed SF State's maximum unit load without advance written approval from the appropriate dean.
Bulletin text: "Under no circumstances is the total unit load for all course registrations in all institutions being attended to exceed the maximum unit load restrictions for this institution without written approval in advance from either the dean of Undergraduate Education and Academic Planning or the dean of Graduate Studies."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Enrollment Verification > Financial Aid

title: GE 'met in the major'
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: GE 'met in the major' (undergraduate students)

Some majors satisfy specific GE areas ('met in the major') once the listed courses are completed, whether or not the student finishes the major.
Bulletin text: "This is true whether or not the student completes the major."
Source: Met in Major >

title: Can seniors take graduate courses
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Can seniors take graduate courses (undergraduate students)

Seniors may enroll in graduate courses only with the instructor's special permission.
Bulletin text: "Seniors may enroll in graduate courses only with special permission of the instructor."
Source: Graduation and Commencement > Courses in Excess of Bachelor’s Degree Requirements

title: Census date: when you count as enrolled (20th day)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Census date: when you count as enrolled (20th day) (all students)

To count as attending a semester, a student must be enrolled in at least one class on the 20th day of instruction (10th day of each summer session).
Bulletin text: "To be considered in attendance for any semester, the student must be reported as enrolled in at least one class on the 20th day of instruction in the fall and spring semesters and the 10th day of instruction in each session of the Regular session summer semester."
Source: Policies and Procedures > Classification of Students for Registration > Continuing

title: Graduate-level units required on the ATC (50%)
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Graduate-level units required on the ATC (50%) (graduate students)

At least 50% of Advancement to Candidacy units must be graduate-level (700-999) courses.
Bulletin text: "Fifty percent (50%) of the units from exclusively graduate-level courses (700-999 level)."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > The Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) > Advancement to Candidacy (ATC) Requirements

title: Continuous enrollment while finishing a thesis/culminating experience
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Continuous enrollment while finishing a thesis/culminating experience (graduate students)

Graduate students who haven't finished their Culminating Experience by the end of the following ('grace') semester must enroll in a zero-unit CPaGE course every semester until they finish.
Bulletin text: "Students who do not complete their Culminating Experience during the semester of enrollment in the Culminating Experience or the following semester, excluding winter and summer, (the “grace” semester) must enroll in a zero-unit course with the College of Professional & Global Education (CPaGL) and every subsequent semester until the Culminating Experience is completed."
Source: Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures > Culminating Experience > Continuous Enrollment in Culminating Experience

title: Course numbering: lower-division, upper-division, graduate
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Academic rule: Course numbering: lower-division, upper-division, graduate (all students)

text:

Description: Reflect on an internship or experiential learning experience and build career readiness skills. title: A U 400 Peer Mentoring
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course A U 400: Peer Mentoring

A U 400 — Peer Mentoring (3 units)
Subject: All University (A U) | Level: upper-division
Prerequisite: Upper-division standing.
Description: Explore theories and concepts of peer mentoring and evidence-based studies on the impact of peer mentoring on student success. Develop an understanding of and practice using inclusive classroom and communication strategies that will facilitate student development, academic skills, and community building to effectively support students transitioning into higher education. Apply understandings of peer mentoring in different settings, including first-year seminars, new student orientation, and the transfer student transition. May be repeated for a total of 6 units.
Topics: Peer Mentoring: First-Year Experience; Student Leaders for New Student Orientation; Peer Mentoring for Transfer Students

title: AA S 108 Asian American Artistic Explorations: Creativity, Identity, and Community
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course AA S 108: Asian American Artistic Explorations: Creativity, Identity, and Community

AA S 108 — Asian American Artistic Explorations: Creativity, Identity, and Community (3 units)
Subject: Asian American Studies (AA S) | Level: lower-division
Prerequisite: GE Area 1A/A2*.
Description: Examine Asian American artistic explorations as self-expression, a reflection of community, and a tool for organizing. Study how artists utilize creative work for the exploration, recording, understanding, and expression of Asian American life. Investigate the importance of visual literacy in enacting social justice and empowerment in the Asian American community. Explore how Asian American artists employ autobiography and self-portraiture to analyze and express concerns such as well-being, identity formation, social justice, and community activism. Analyze works by Asian American creators in relation to the Asian American community. Writing and creative assignments. (Plus-minus letter grade only)
Grading: Plus-minus letter grade only

text:

Description: Exploration of the various meanings attributed to the Nation of Islam (NOI) cultural and religious practices. Emphasis on the ways in which the NOI's ideological structure has allowed it to function in the context of Black education. Examination of the lives of such figures as Wallace D. Fard, Elijah Muhammad, Malcolm X, and Louis Farrakhan. Other themes covered include: Five Percenters, Elijah Muhammad Studies, the NOI teachings in Popular Culture, the role of women in the NOI, the NOI's California connection, and the NOI and critical pedagogy.

Subject: Africana Studies (AFRS) | Level: upper-division
Prerequisite: Upper-division standing.
Description: A close examination of author, activist, playwright, and feminist Lorraine Hansberry's life and work in literature, Civil Rights, Feminist Advocacies, The Black Arts Movement, and her journey towards iconic status as a woman of prolific artistry, her emergence as a feminist, an anti-racism activist, and warrior for human rights. Dramaturgical studies explore the biography "Looking for Lorraine" by Imani Perry, as well as her speeches, poetry, articles, and recordings of interviews. This examination will culminate in a performance of Hansberry's play "To Be Young, Gifted and Black."

title: AIS 250 American Indian Populations and Colonial Diseases
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course AIS 250: American Indian Populations and Colonial Diseases

AIS 250 — American Indian Populations and Colonial Diseases (3 units)
Subject: American Indian Studies (AIS) | Level: lower-division
Prerequisite: Category I or II placement for QR/Math or satisfactory completion of ELM requirement, or MATH 70 or ESM 70 with a grade of C or better. Category III or IV placement for QR/Math or students who have not passed MATH 70 or ESM 70 with a C or better must be concurrently enrolled in MATH 122 or MATH 123.
May be taken concurrently (co-enrollment allowed): MATH 122
Description: A historical overview of the relationships between American Indian populations changes and colonial diseases experienced by major indigenous cultures and peoples residing within the present-day boundaries of the United States from contact through 1930. title: ANTH 100 Introduction to Biological Anthropology
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course ANTH 100: Introduction to Biological Anthropology

ANTH 100 — Introduction to Biological Anthropology (3 units)
Subject: Anthropology (ANTH) | Level: lower-division
Prerequisites: none listed
Description: Overview of the scientific evidence for the origin and evolution of the human species. Examine the biological and behavioral diversity of living and past human populations and the closest mammalian relatives - the non-human primates. Introduction to topics that include natural selection and the mechanisms of evolution; molecular and population genetics; primate diversity and behavior; the fossil record of human evolution, behavior, and ecology; and human biocultural adaptation.

title: ANTH 301 Foundations of Archaeology
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course ANTH 301: Foundations of Archaeology

ANTH 301 — Foundations of Archaeology (3 units)
Subject: Anthropology (ANTH) | Level: upper-division
Prerequisite: Upper-division standing; ANTH 110; or permission of the instructor.
Description: Examine the history of archaeological thinking from the antiquarians of the Middle Ages to today's use of archaeology by modern politicians and activists. How do people use sites, artifacts, monuments, burials, and art to construct accurate histories and prehistories? What theories and philosophical approaches help people understand the archaeological record? Is archaeology a hard science based on objective facts, or is it a social science that uses subjective knowledge? How do people know what they know about their own and other peoples' past? (Plus-minus letter grade only)
Grading: Plus-minus letter grade only
Is a prerequisite for: ANTH 695
Listed in program requirements of: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology

title: ANTH 631 STEM and Social Justice
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course ANTH 631: STEM and Social Justice

ANTH 631 — STEM and Social Justice (3 units)
Subject: Anthropology (ANTH) | Level: upper-division
Prerequisite: Restricted to upper-division standing; GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better; or permission of the instructor.
Description: Introduction to the anthropology of society, technology, and medicine (STM) and to the field of science and technology studies (STS). Key themes include the history of studying STM in Anthropology, theoretical concepts in STS, and the critical evaluation of case studies. Topics and case studies to be addressed include indigenous science, race and gender in STM fields, anthropological studies of science and scientists, biomedicine and biotechnology, the social consequences of computational algorithms, surveillance technology and privacy rights, work and class in online 'platform' economies, STM and identity, and the social justice dimensions of STM.
General Education areas: 4UD: Social/Behavioral Science; UD-D: Social Sciences
SF State Studies: Social Justice
Listed in program requirements of: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology; Certificate in Ethnography; Certificate in Global Health

Recommended (not required) preparation: ARTH 202
Description: Overview of modern and contemporary art since 1945 as it has been practiced and exhibited in the North American and Western European art world. Introduction to canonical and non-canonical modern and contemporary works of art. Emphasis on the ways in which art and art history engage with social and political processes. Themes and topics include abstraction, artistic medium, pop art, minimalism, site-specificity, earth art, conceptual art, performance art, video art, queer and feminist practices, politics of identity, appropriation, social practice, activist art, globalization, art and climate change, and art and disability.

text:

ASTR 340GW — The Big Bang - GWAR (3 units)
Subject: Astronomy (ASTR) | Level: upper-division
Prerequisite: GE Area 1A/A2 and PHYS 320 with a grade of C- or better.
Description: Introduction to cosmology from earlier human conceptions of the universe through the hot Big Bang. Topics include: measuring space and time, the cosmic distance ladder, gravitation, general relativity and the curvature of spacetime, expansion of the universe, large scale structure, the early universe, the cosmic microwave background, nucleosynthesis, dark matter, dark energy and the ultimate fate of the universe. Emphasis will be on how we know what we know about the universe, including observational and experimental evidence. (ABC/NC grading only)
Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR).
Other attributes: Graduation Writing Assessment
Grading: ABC/NC grading only

Description: Legal, ethical, and normative questions in the work of journalists and media organizations are examined in case studies from Israel, the U.S., and the U.K. by analyzing the media's relationships with the political arena, the private sector, and security forces. Description: Examine the cultural, ethical, economic, and political dimensions of science, technology, and health in a global context. Explore how science, technology, and public health both shape politics and are shaped by politics. Consider the role of science in government and society; the dilemmas of international organizations and scientific knowledge; technology and big tech companies in international relations, science and technology policy, and government regulation; global health regimes and institutions; and the implications of social media, artificial intelligence, and cyber-currencies. (This course is offered as I R 305 and BIOL 305. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

Description: Non-technical survey of the global microfinance industry, which provides financial services to the poor on a large scale, mostly in developing nations. Historical origins and industry evolution. Nature and developmental role of microenterprises and informal finance. Methods and technologies used by microfinance institutions (MFIs). Case studies of leading MFIs and the lives of their clients. Policy and regulatory environments. Debates over profiting from the poor, and over health and environmental goals. Prerequisite: Restricted to Criminal Justice Studies majors and minors.

Prerequisite: GE Areas 1A/A2*, 1B/A3*, 1C/A1*, and 2/B4* all with grades of C- or better or permission of the instructor.
Description: Examine the strange, tumultuous, and sometimes cruel period of reentry after incarceration. Explore current approaches to re-entry, focusing on the key element of housing. A critical look at dated and current theories concerning re-integration/integration, examining theories inspired by medical, social, and criminology models. Critically examine current practices of reentry, which tend towards a one size fits all (cookie-cutter) approach. Lecture, 2 units; activity, 1 unit. (This course is offered as SOC 511, C J 511, and USP 511. Students may not repeat the course under an alternate prefix.)

text:

Explore classic works of practical effects pioneers such as Georges Méliès and stop-motion animator Willis O'Brien, as well as the latest innovations by digital visual effects powerhouses such as ILM, Digital Domain, and Weta Digital. Discussions on contemporary trends and recent developments in the global VFX industry.

title: CLAS 701 Greek Language and Literature
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course CLAS 701: Greek Language and Literature

CLAS 701 — Greek Language and Literature (3 units)
Subject: Classics (CLAS) | Level: graduate
Prerequisite: Graduate Classics students or permission of the instructor.
Description: Survey of the major texts, key themes, and methods at the core of the study of Greek language and literature. Overview of the ways modern scholarship on Greek language and literature has evolved methodologically and theoretically, and how other, related disciplines inform and have been informed by such scholarship. Focus extends from Homer to the authors of the Common Era. Discussion of poetry in a range of meters, prose texts, contexts of composition and performance, and audience reception.

Subject: Classics (CLAS) | Level: graduate
Prerequisite: Graduate Classics students or permission of the instructor.

title: CLAS 704 Roman Art and Archaeology
text:
[SFSU Bulletin 2026-2027] Course CLAS 704: Roman Art and Archaeology

CLAS 704 — Roman Art and Archaeology (3 units)
Subject: Classics (CLAS) | Level: graduate
Prerequisite: Graduate Classics students or permission of the instructor.
Description: Graduate foundational study of the discipline of Roman art and archaeology, including use of primary ancient sources (in original and translation), the historical framework, epigraphy, numismatics, ceramic analysis, major Roman archaeological sites in Italy and throughout the empire, and approaches to the study of artifacts and Roman ceramics. The use of 3D reconstruction, Geographical Information Systems (GIS), typology, and data management are explored. Includes hands-on practice of academic publication and conference presentation skills.
Listed in program requirements of: Master of Arts in Classics
